instructions:
1. Grasp a pull-up bar with an underhand grip, hands closer than shoulder-width.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and legs crossed behind you.
3. Pull your shoulder blades down to start the movement.
4. Drive your elbows down and pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. The narrow grip loads the biceps hard, so keep the pull smooth without swinging.
2. Lower slowly to keep tension on the lats and biceps.
3. Keep your shoulders pulled away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Grasp a pull-up bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and legs crossed behind you.
3. Pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the movement.
4. Bend your elbows and pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lead with the elbows and drive them down toward your ribs.
2. Lower slowly to maximise muscle activation.
3. Keep your shoulders pulled away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:

2. Hang with arms fully extended and legs crossed behind you.
3. Pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the movement.
4. Bend your elbows and pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. The wider grip shifts emphasis to the lats and upper back.
2. Drive your elbows down and squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
3. Lower slowly and keep your shoulders away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Grasp a parallel-grip handle with palms facing each other, hands close together.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and legs crossed behind you.
3. Pull your shoulder blades down to start the movement.
4. Bend your elbows and pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
5. Lower under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. The neutral grip is shoulder-friendly and loads the biceps and brachialis hard.
2. Drive your elbows straight down and keep your torso steady.
3. Lower slowly and keep your shoulders away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up and inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your arms and place your fingertips on your shoulders, elbows pointing out.
3. Draw circles with your elbows, moving them forward, up, back, and down.
4. Keep the motion smooth and controlled.
5. After several circles, reverse the direction.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly to improve shoulder mobility and control.
2. Keep your shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
3. Keep your core braced so your torso stays still.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the movement.
